thm:brick-diminimal.label: thm:brick-diminimal
thm:brick-diminimal.text: Let $S$ be a seed of diameter $d$ and suppose that there exists a brick $M\in\mathcal{S}(S)$ with respect to some main root $r$ of $S$. Then every matrix in any sequence of regular diameter-preserving ABDs starting with $M$ has the same set of distinct eigenvalues as $M$. In particular, $S$ is diminimal.

def:brick.label: def:brick
def:brick.text: Let $T$ be a tree with diameter $d$, rooted at a main root $r$, and let $M\in\mathcal{S}(T)$. We say that $M$ is a brick (with respect to $r$) if $q(M)=d+1$ and $\Delta(M)=\Delta_c(M)$, that is, if $M$ has the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues allowed by Theorem 3.2 and all its latent values are confined.

prop:tower-bricks.label: prop:tower-bricks
prop:tower-bricks.text: Let $k\geq 3$, let $T$ be one of the trees $S^{(i,j)}_{2k+1}$, for $1\leq i,j\leq 6$, and $S^{[b]}_{2k+1}$, for $4\leq b\leq k$, with towers $H$ and $H'$ whose base pairs have depths $h-1$ and $h$, rooted at $r$ and $r'$, let $\tL_h$ be a set of $2h+1$ real numbers, let $e>\lmax{h}$ be a real number, let the $\ell_j$ be as in (6.14), and let $c<\lmin{k}$. If neither call below returns $\bot$, then { $\begin{aligned} M=\varphi\Bigl(&TowerChain\bigl(H,\tL_h,(\ell_{h+1},\ldots,\ell_k)\bigr),\\ &TowerChain\bigl(H',\tL'_h,(\ell_{h+2},\ldots,\ell_{k+1})\bigr),\,c\Bigr) \end{aligned}$ } is a brick of $T$ with respect to $r$, with $\mathcal Z(M)=\{c\}\cup\tL'_k\cup\{\lmin{k}+\lmaxp{k}-c\}$ and $\Delta(M)=\{\lmaxp{k}\}$. Moreover, each of these trees admits, with respect to each of its two main roots, a brick whose set of latent values has a single element.

many_seeds.label: many_seeds
many_seeds.text: For every odd $d\geq 7$ there are at least $21+(d-7)/2$ pairwise non-isomorphic diminimal seeds of diameter $d$, and for every even $d\geq 8$ there are at least $36+(d-8)/2$. In particular, the number of diminimal seeds of diameter $d$ tends to infinity as $d\to\infty$.

thm:C.label: thm:C
thm:C.text: For every $d\geq 1$, almost every set of $d+1$ real numbers is the set of distinct eigenvalues of a brick of $S_d$.

lem:six-arms.label: lem:six-arms
lem:six-arms.text: Let $\Lambda=\{\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_6\}$, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, and suppose that the following conditions hold, where $\gamma_L=\lambda_1-\lambda_0$ and $\gamma_R=\lambda_6-\lambda_5$ are the outer gaps of $\Lambda$, $\mu_-=\lambda_0+\lambda_6-\lambda_5$, $\mu_+=\lambda_0+\lambda_6-\lambda_1$, and $\Lambda_-=\{\mu_-,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_4\}$ and $\Lambda_+=\{\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_5,\mu_+\}$ are the lateral sets of $\Lambda$: (C1) for $i=1,2$: $\lambda_6=\lambda_1+\lambda_5-\lambda_0$; (C2) for $i=2,3,5$: $\lambda_1+\lambda_5=\lambda_2+\lambda_4$; (C3) for $i=3,4,5$: $\gamma_L\neq\gamma_R$; (C4) for $i=3,4$: $\mu_-+\lambda_4=\lambda_1+\lambda_3$ if $\gamma_L>\gamma_R$, and $\lambda_2+\mu_+=\lambda_3+\lambda_5$ if $\gamma_R>\gamma_L$; (C5) for $i=5$: $\Lambda_-$ is admissible if $\gamma_L>\gamma_R$, and $\Lambda_+$ is admissible if $\gamma_R>\gamma_L$; (C6) for $i=1,4$: $\{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_5\}$ is admissible, and for $i=6$: $\Lambda$ is admissible. Then there is a tight strong realization of $\Lambda$ in $\{R_i\}$, rooted at the root of $R_i$.
